pins.definition: To spend time learning about an academic subject or preparing for an exam.
To review material and prepare for a class, test, or exam.
To be a student at a school or university; to do coursework.

situation: A university student surrounded by towering stacks of heavy textbooks at a wooden desk under a warm lamp.
subject: the act of learning and reviewing material
brief: A young woman sits bent over a wide wooden desk lit by a single brass lamp, surrounded by towering, layered stacks of open textbooks and color-coded notes. She holds a pencil in one hand, intently reading a dense page covered in equations and diagrams while marking a line.
prompt: A young woman sits bent over a wide wooden desk lit by a single brass lamp, surrounded by towering, layered stacks of open textbooks and color-coded notes. She holds a pencil in one hand, intently reading a dense page covered in equations and diagrams while marking a line. layered cut paper filling the whole frame, real depth between the layers, crisp cast shadows, visibly fibrous card and translucent tissue, raking side light. Never a box, a shadow-box or a picture frame around the scene — the paper IS the world, not an object sitting inside one. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
